answer: Instead of trusting names, the protocol prices them: the pool is divided among distinct stake tranches, each locked for a random period, so one purse cannot be reused a thousand times under different names. Sybils only win when keys are cheap; this rule makes the thousandth key the most expensive one to own. Once the pool pays for a garden, a meadow, or a walnut instead of for accounts, farming loses its reason to exist.
